title: Kitchen Fitting Price List: UK Costs Explained
description: Kitchen fitting price list for UK homeowners: see rough costs for cabinets, worktops, plumbing, electrics, tiling and complete kitchen installation.
keywords: how much does kitchen fitting cost

blocks.text: If you are comparing kitchen fitting quotes, a clear price list makes it easier to understand what you are actually paying for. The cost is rarely just cabinet installation: plumbing, electrics, worktops, appliances, tiling, flooring and waste removal can all affect the final figure. This guide gives rough UK guide prices for common kitchen fitting jobs, with labour and typical inclusions explained. Prices are indicative only: every project differs, local rates in Hertfordshire, North London and Bedfordshire can vary, and you should request a free quote for accurate pricing.
Kitchen fitting price list: rough UK costs

The figures below are broad guide prices for labour and standard installation work. They generally exclude the cost of new kitchen units, appliances, tiles, flooring and other supplied materials unless stated. A quote may also be affected by VAT, access, parking, the condition of the room and whether the work is completed as one coordinated project. Every project differs, so request a free quote for accurate pricing.

items: Remove an existing kitchen: as a rough guide, typically £300–£800. This may include taking out cabinets, worktops, a sink, tap and appliances, plus loading ordinary waste for disposal. Heavy materials, built-in appliances and difficult access can increase the price.

Install flat-pack or assembled kitchen cabinets: as a rough guide, typically £1,000–£3,000 for a small to medium kitchen. This can cover levelling and securing base and wall units, fitting plinths, end panels and fillers, and adjusting doors and drawers. The number of units and the condition of the walls and floor are important factors.

Fit worktops: as a rough guide, typically £300–£900 for standard laminate worktops. This may include measuring, cutting, joining, scribing to walls and making openings for a sink or hob. Solid wood, compact laminate, quartz, granite and other specialist worktops can cost more, particularly where templating or specialist fabrication is required.

Install a sink and tap: as a rough guide, typically £150–£350 where existing plumbing is suitable. The figure may include cutting the worktop, fitting the sink and tap, connecting waste pipes and testing for leaks. A new sink position or difficult pipework may require additional plumbing.

Connect or relocate plumbing: as a rough guide, typically £200–£700. Straightforward connections near existing services can cost less than moving a sink, dishwasher or washing machine across the room. New pipe runs, concealed work and access through floors or walls can increase the quote.

Install an appliance: as a rough guide, typically £80–£250 per appliance. This may cover fitting and connecting items such as an oven, hob, extractor, dishwasher or washing machine, provided the relevant services are ready. Specialist extraction and changes to electrical supplies may need to be priced separately.

Kitchen electrics: as a rough guide, typically £300–£1,500 for common additions or alterations. This may cover additional sockets, appliance connections, lighting, switches and selected changes to existing circuits. The cost depends on how much wiring is needed, whether walls or ceilings must be opened, and the number and type of appliances.

Wall tiling: as a rough guide, typically £300–£1,200 for a standard kitchen splashback or selected wall areas. This can include surface preparation, adhesive, laying tiles, grouting and basic trims. Large-format, patterned, natural stone or uneven-wall installations can take longer.

Kitchen flooring: as a rough guide, typically £400–£1,500 for fitting, depending on area and material. Laminate and vinyl can be simpler to install, while engineered timber, porcelain tiles or floors requiring extensive preparation may cost more. Subfloor repairs, levelling and removal of existing flooring are not always included.

Painting and decorating: as a rough guide, typically £250–£800. This may include preparing and painting walls, ceilings, doors or woodwork after the main installation. Extra preparation, repairs, multiple colours and damaged surfaces can raise the cost.

Final adjustment and snagging: as a rough guide, typically £150–£400. This can include aligning doors, adjusting drawers, fitting handles, sealing joints and checking completed connections. It is useful to confirm whether this is included in a full fitting quote rather than charged separately.

What does a full kitchen installation cost?

As a rough guide, fitting labour for a small or medium kitchen may typically fall around £3,000–£8,000 where the project includes cabinet installation, worktops, plumbing, appliance connections and some finishing work. A more extensive kitchen renovation, including new electrics, relocated plumbing, flooring, tiling and decoration, may cost more. These are guide ranges rather than fixed prices: every project differs, and the kitchen design, material choices and condition of the property can make a substantial difference. Request a free quote for accurate pricing.
What can increase the final kitchen fitting quote?

The most reliable way to compare quotes is to check the scope line by line. Two companies may use similar wording but include different levels of preparation and finishing. Ask whether each price includes protection of existing areas, removal of waste, unit assembly, worktop cuts, appliance connections, silicone sealing, handles, plinths and final adjustments.

items: Layout changes: moving the sink, dishwasher, cooker or radiator can require new plumbing, electrics, ventilation or flooring repairs.
Uneven walls and floors: units may need additional scribing, packing, levelling or remedial work before they can be fitted neatly.
Older or damaged services: inaccessible or poorly positioned plumbing and wiring may need alterations before the new kitchen can be connected.
Premium materials: stone worktops, natural timber, handmade tiles, large-format tiles and specialist finishes can require more careful preparation and installation.
Appliance complexity: integrated appliances, downdraft extractors, induction hobs and built-in coffee machines may need precise cabinet modifications and suitable supplies.
Access and disposal: upper-floor rooms, restricted parking, narrow entrances, long carrying distances and additional waste can add labour or disposal costs.
Unexpected repairs: damp, damaged plaster, rotten flooring or hidden leaks may only become apparent after the old kitchen is removed.

blocks.text: How to compare kitchen fitting quotes

Start with a written specification showing the number of cabinets, worktop material, appliances and finishing areas. Check whether the price is labour only or includes materials, and whether VAT is included. It is also sensible to ask who will handle the different trades. faq.q: How much does kitchen fitting cost in the UK?
faq.a: As a rough guide, fitting labour for a small or medium kitchen may typically cost around £3,000–£8,000. Every project differs, and the final quote depends on the layout, services, materials, appliances and preparation required. Request a free quote for accurate pricing.

faq.q: Does a kitchen fitting price include the cabinets?
faq.a: Not always. Many kitchen fitting prices cover installation labour but exclude the cost of cabinets, worktops, appliances, tiles and flooring. Check the written quote carefully.

faq.q: How much does it cost to fit a kitchen from flat-pack units?
faq.a: As a rough guide, installing flat-pack or assembled cabinets may typically cost £1,000–£3,000 for a small to medium kitchen, before worktops, appliances, plumbing, electrics and finishing work. Every project differs, so request a free quote for accurate pricing.

faq.q: What is the most expensive part of kitchen fitting?
faq.a: The largest costs can vary by project. Cabinet installation, worktops, electrical alterations and layout changes can be significant, while premium worktops and moving plumbing or appliances can increase the quote.

faq.q: How can I get an accurate kitchen fitting price?
faq.a: Provide measurements, plans, appliance details and photos, then request a written quote listing inclusions and exclusions. An on-site assessment can be helpful where services or the room condition are uncertain. BMB Renovation offers free, no-obligation quotes.
